alerts.reason: Year-over-year sales growth slipped from +0.60% in December to -0.43% in March. Higher prices and product mix cushioned a decline in units, and pricing accounted for the nine-month sales gain (A, B, D). I expect pricing to keep June above -5%, then provide too little support to prevent a decline of at least 5% in July–September.

Revenue growth slowed from 95.23% in December to 36.84% in March. Distribution gains still supported shipments, but the largest distributor reduced inventory days in North America, which accounted for $339.5 million of $355.7 million in March revenue (A–C). I expect June growth to remain above -5%. The July–September crossing depends on that distributor cutting orders faster than new distribution adds sales.

If growth slows by roughly the same 5.7 percentage points in each of the next two quarters as those contributions fade, June stays above -5% and July–September falls below it.

Lower customer prices and deliberate volume cuts at plants undergoing turnarounds could persist. From March, only another 0.37 percentage points of decline would put July–September below the threshold (A, D).

I expect the remaining orders to support June sales above -5%, with fewer back orders available to sustain shipments in July–September.

Cerence accelerated $67.8 million of deferred revenue into December, more than the $54.1 million increase for the entire six-month period. March revenue was already down 0.83% year over year (A–C). I forecast June above -5% and July–September at or below -5%. The timing depends on how much revenue would otherwise have been recognized in each quarter.

The consolidated revenue decline widened from 0.80% in December to 3.52% in March. Applebee’s domestic same-restaurant sales fell 4.6%, and Dine Brands reported lower franchise and rental revenue (A, B). I expect June to remain above -5%, with persistent restaurant weakness pushing the consolidated decline to at least 5% in July–September.

For the regional fleet discussed in C, asset dispositions reduced charter revenue by $0.9 million, absorbing most of the $1.3 million gain from higher rates and utilization.
